subject: biology-1
question: A cell in a sealed chamber uses up all of its oxygen, and the electron transport chain shuts down within seconds. What is the direct role of oxygen in the chain?

options.text: Oxygen is the final electron acceptor, becoming water, so electrons can no longer flow when it is gone.
Oxygen is the first electron donor, becoming CO2, so no electrons enter the chain when it is gone.
Oxygen pumps protons across the inner membrane, so the gradient collapses without it.
Oxygen carries electrons from glycolysis to the chain, so delivery halts without it.

explanation: At the end of the chain, oxygen accepts electrons and combines with protons to form water, and this keeps the chain running by clearing electrons. B reverses the roles of electron donor and acceptor. C confuses oxygen with the pumping complexes. D confuses oxygen with the carrier molecules NADH and FADH2.
